q: How many employees are former (left_date is not NULL)? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees WHERE left_date IS NOT NULL

q: How many former employees are in each department? Include departments with zero. Return department name and count.
gold: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS n FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = d.id AND e.left_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.name

q: What is the average current salary among former employees? Current salary = the salary row with the latest effective_from. Return a single number rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold: WITH cur AS (SELECT employee_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from DESC) AS rn FROM salaries) SELECT ROUND(AVG(cur.amount), 2) AS v FROM cur JOIN employees e ON e.id = cur.employee_id WHERE cur.rn = 1 AND e.left_date IS NOT NULL

q: Which department has the highest average current salary among its former employees (current salary = latest effective_from)? Return the department name; on ties the alphabetically first.
gold: WITH cur AS (SELECT employee_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from DESC) AS rn FROM salaries) SELECT d.name FROM cur JOIN employees e ON e.id = cur.employee_id JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id WHERE cur.rn = 1 AND e.left_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY AVG(cur.amount) DESC, d.name LIMIT 1

q: What is the average review score per department for review_year 2023, counting only departments with at least 3 reviews that year? Return department name and average score.
gold: SELECT d.name, AVG(r.score) AS avg_score FROM reviews r JOIN employees e ON e.id = r.employee_id JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id WHERE r.review_year = 2023 GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3

q: For each current manager, count their current direct reports. Return the top 1 managers as (manager name, count), ordered by count descending, then manager id ascending.
gold: SELECT m.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id WHERE e.left_date IS NULL AND m.left_date IS NULL GROUP BY m.id, m.name ORDER BY n DESC, m.id LIMIT 1

q: Which former employee has the largest salary increase (current salary with the latest effective_from minus the first salary with the earliest effective_from)? Return employee id and the increase; on ties the lowest id.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT employee_id, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from DESC) AS rd, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id ORDER BY effective_from ASC) AS ra FROM salaries), c AS (SELECT employee_id, amount FROM s WHERE rd = 1), f AS (SELECT employee_id, amount FROM s WHERE ra = 1) SELECT e.id, c.amount - f.amount AS increase FROM employees e JOIN c ON c.employee_id = e.id JOIN f ON f.employee_id = e.id WHERE e.left_date IS NOT NULL ORDER BY increase DESC, e.id LIMIT 1

q: Departments form a tree via parent_id with 'Corporate' at the root. For each department directly under Corporate, count the former employees in it and all its descendant departments. Return department name and headcount.
gold: WITH RECURSIVE t AS (SELECT id, name AS top_name FROM departments WHERE parent_id = (SELECT id FROM departments WHERE name = 'Corporate') UNION ALL SELECT d.id, t.top_name FROM departments d JOIN t ON d.parent_id = t.id) SELECT t.top_name AS name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount FROM t LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.dept_id = t.id AND e.left_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.top_name

q: Among employees hired before 2021-01-01, what percentage left within 730 days of their hire date (left_date - hire_date <= 730)? Return a single number rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN left_date IS NOT NULL AND left_date - hire_date <= 730 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM employees WHERE hire_date < DATE '2021-01-01'

q: How many orders have status 'cancelled'? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'

q: For orders with status 'cancelled' only, what is the number of order lines per customer country (NULL countries excluded)? Return country and the value.
gold: SELECT c.country, COUNT(*) AS v FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' AND c.country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.country

q: Which 3 customers have the highest total revenue from 'cancelled' orders (sum of quantity * order_items.unit_price)? Return customer id and total, highest first; on ties the lower id first.
gold: SELECT c.id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id ORDER BY total DESC, c.id LIMIT 3

q: How many 'cancelled' orders contain at least one order line with quantity 5? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.id AND oi.quantity = 5)

q: For each customer, find the date of their first 'cancelled' order. Then count customers by the calendar year of that date. Return year and count.
gold: WITH f AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(order_date) AS d FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM d) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS n FROM f GROUP BY yr

q: What is the average 'cancelled' order value (an order's value is the sum of quantity * order_items.unit_price over its lines) per customer country, only for countries with at least 10 such orders and excluding NULL countries? Return country and average value.

q: How many users on the 'free' plan have no sessions at all? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users u WHERE u.plan = 'free' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id)

q: For each user with at least one session, take the device of their earliest session (earliest started_at, then lowest session id). Count 'free' users by that first device. Return device and count.
gold: WITH f AS (SELECT s.user_id, s.device, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY s.started_at, s.id) AS rn FROM sessions s) SELECT f.device, COUNT(*) AS n FROM f JOIN users u ON u.id = f.user_id WHERE f.rn = 1 AND u.plan = 'free' GROUP BY f.device

q: What percentage of 'ios' sessions contain at least one 'click' event? Return a single number rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e WHERE e.session_id = s.id AND e.kind = 'click') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM sessions s WHERE s.device = 'ios'

q: How many 'free' users made their first 'click' event in a session that was not their first session? Order sessions by started_at then session id; a user's first 'click' event is their earliest such event by ts. Return a single number.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT id, user_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY started_at, id) AS rn FROM sessions), p AS (SELECT s.user_id, s.rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY e.ts) AS prn FROM events e JOIN s ON s.id = e.session_id WHERE e.kind = 'click') SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.user_id WHERE p.prn = 1 AND p.rn > 1 AND u.plan = 'free'

q: What is the total purchase amount (sum of value over 'purchase' events) for users on the 'pro' plan? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(e.value), 0) AS total FROM events e JOIN sessions s ON s.id = e.session_id JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id WHERE e.kind = 'purchase' AND u.plan = 'pro'

q: How many users on the 'pro' plan have no sessions at all? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users u WHERE u.plan = 'pro' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions s WHERE s.user_id = u.id)

q: For each user with at least one session, take the device of their earliest session (earliest started_at, then lowest session id). Count 'pro' users by that first device. Return device and count.

q: What percentage of 'ios' sessions contain at least one 'purchase' event? Return a single number rounded to 2 decimal places.
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events e WHERE e.session_id = s.id AND e.kind = 'purchase') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM sessions s WHERE s.device = 'ios'

q: What is the median number of events per session, over sessions that have at least one event? Return a single number.
gold: WITH c AS (SELECT session_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events GROUP BY session_id) SELECT MEDIAN(n) AS v FROM c

q: How many 'pro' users made their first 'purchase' event in a session that was not their first session? Order sessions by started_at then session id; a user's first 'purchase' event is their earliest such event by ts. Return a single number.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT id, user_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY started_at, id) AS rn FROM sessions), p AS (SELECT s.user_id, s.rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.user_id ORDER BY e.ts) AS prn FROM events e JOIN s ON s.id = e.session_id WHERE e.kind = 'purchase') SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM p JOIN users u ON u.id = p.user_id WHERE p.prn = 1 AND p.rn > 1 AND u.plan = 'pro'

q: Bucket sessions by the week they started (DATE_TRUNC('week', started_at)). Which week had the most distinct active users? Return the week start as a date and the user count; on ties the earliest week.
gold: SELECT CAST(DATE_TRUNC('week', started_at) AS DATE) AS b, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS n FROM sessions GROUP BY b ORDER BY n DESC, b LIMIT 1

q: For orders with status 'refunded' only, what is the average line value (quantity * order_items.unit_price) per customer country (NULL countries excluded)? Return country and the value.
gold: SELECT c.country, AVG(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS v FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'refunded' AND c.country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.country

q: How many 'refunded' orders contain at least one order line with quantity 1? Return a single number.
gold: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'refunded' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.id AND oi.quantity = 1)

q: How many customers placed their second 'refunded' order within 14 days (inclusive) of their first 'refunded' order? Order by order_date, then order id, to rank orders. Return a single number.
gold: WITH s AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS rn FROM orders WHERE status = 'refunded'), f AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date AS d1 FROM s WHERE rn = 1), g AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date AS d2 FROM s WHERE rn = 2) SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM f JOIN g USING (customer_id) WHERE d2 - d1 <= 14

q: What is the average 'refunded' order value (an order's value is the sum of quantity * order_items.unit_price over its lines) per customer country, only for countries with at least 5 such orders and excluding NULL countries? Return country and average value.
gold: WITH ov AS (SELECT o.id, c.country, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS v FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'refunded' AND c.country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.id, c.country) SELECT country, AVG(v) AS avg_value FROM ov GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
